solutions.check: 32 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 31 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Green variety of rose ?

parts.note: reads as a pale green kind of rose, but means a leafy green vegetable, which also names a full-headed old rose variety

explanation.walkthrough: The cabbage rose is a real many-petalled rose; the clue asks for a green vegetable that is also a 'variety of rose' by name.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is a green leafy crop, and the same word names the cabbage rose, a densely petalled garden variety.

clue.text: King of infinite space ?

parts.note: a Hamlet line about being king of infinite space, read literally as a ruler of the whole universe

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says he could be 'king of infinite space' in a nutshell; the word wanted is a ruler of the cosmos.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmocrat is a ruler of the world or universe, from Greek cosmos plus kratos, power.

clue.text: It is in the little grey cells the country gets its name

indicators.note: the word it is placed inside the organ that follows

parts.note: Poirot's little grey cells are the brain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims the nation is named after a thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' puts IT inside BRAIN. 'the little grey cells' is detective Poirot's phrase for his brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is the island country made up of England, Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: The scapegoat had its day

parts.note: in Leviticus a goat was sent into the wilderness bearing the people's sins on a Jewish holy day

explanation.walkthrough: The scapegoat ritual belongs to Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is reparation for wrongdoing, and the Jewish fast of Yom Kippur is named the Day of it.

clue.text: Peter's theatrical part in days of yore

indicators.note: part of the words that come before supplies the answer, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Peter once had a role on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' seems to be Peter's acting role but takes a run of letters from inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an old word meaning formerly, long ago.

clue.text: Roped it roughly to the stone

indicators.note: done roughly, the letters of these two words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lashes a load with rope and hauls it carelessly to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges ROPED IT. The page prints 'store', but only 'stone' defines a gem, so the printed word is a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, the gem variety of olivine.

clue.text: "If" is the only one, said Touchstone

definitions.text: "If" is the only one, said Touchstone

parts.words: "If" is the only one, said Touchstone
parts.note: the jester Touchstone in As You Like It praises the word if as the settler of quarrels

explanation.walkthrough: In As You Like It, Touchstone says 'Your If is the only peacemaker; much virtue in If.'
explanation.definitionFit: A peacemaker settles disputes, which Touchstone claims a well-placed 'if' does.

clue.text: Dangers of our policy

parts.note: reads as hazards of a course of action; an insurance policy lists the hazards it covers

explanation.walkthrough: 'policy' suggests a plan of action, but an insurance policy names the risks it covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazards an insurer covers are called by this word, meaning chances of harm.

clue.text: See here !

parts.note: sounds like a call for attention, but a see is a bishop's seat, and this is the area a bishop governs

explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's see is his jurisdiction; the exclamation is a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocese is the district under a bishop, his see.

clue.text: They're cross when at the masthead

definitions.text: They're cross when at the masthead

parts.words: They're cross when at the masthead
parts.note: cross looks like angry, but at the top of a ship's mast are the crosswise timbers

explanation.walkthrough: Crosstrees are horizontal spars at a ship's masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosstrees are the timbers fixed crosswise at the head of a mast.

clue.text: Sounds like a crafty proceeding in Eire

indicators.note: the clue says the place is pronounced like the phrase that follows

parts.note: a crafty proceeding is a sly go, a cunning attempt

explanation.surface: Someone describes an underhand bit of business carried out in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: SLY GO said together gives the Irish town and county.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county and town in the north-west of the Irish Republic, so a place found in Eire.

clue.text: Geological feature of The Wash ?

parts.note: The Wash is an English bay, inviting a coastal rock; read as washing, the rock is the one named after the cleaning bar

explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large bay on England's east coast, so the clue seems to want its geology; but the wash is also laundry, needing soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapstone, or steatite, is a soft talc-rich rock that feels soapy to the touch.

clue.text: Go near the animal if you want to upset it

indicators.note: upsetting these words tips their letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to approach a beast if you want to annoy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' sounds like annoying the beast, but it rearranges GO NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of Asia, a hoofed beast.

clue.text: They show no respect for their betters

definitions.text: They show no respect for their betters

parts.words: They show no respect for their betters
parts.note: reads as insolent underlings; betters are really people who place bets, whom these bookmakers fail to pay

explanation.walkthrough: 'Betters' means social superiors on the surface but people who bet underneath; a welsher is a bookmaker who runs off without paying out.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh is to dodge paying a betting debt, so these defaulters disregard the punters they owe.

clue.text: A steady worker with the horses

definitions.text: A steady worker with the horses

parts.note: stable means steady or firm
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the job as well as building it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablehand is a groom employed to look after horses.

clue.text: Woman artist born to rule

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist
née marks a maiden name, meaning born

explanation.surface: A female painter is said to be destined to govern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rule' adds colour: a ranee rules as a rajah's wife or a queen in her own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranee is an Indian queen or princess, a female ruler or a rajah's wife.

clue.text: Shakespearian doll

parts.note: doll looks like a toy, but is a woman's name: the Doll who appears in Shakespeare's history plays

explanation.walkthrough: Doll Tearsheet is the tavern woman in Henry IV Part 2.
explanation.definitionFit: The character's full name in the play is Doll Tearsheet, Falstaff's companion at the Boar's Head.

clue.text: This compartment doesn't appear to be full

definitions.text: This compartment doesn't appear to be full

parts.words: This compartment doesn't appear to be full
parts.note: split, the words say there is space yet; together they name a storeroom for preserves and liqueurs

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, STILL ROOM says there is space left; joined, it is a household room where cordials were distilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A stillroom is a room in a large house for distilling, preserving and storing food and drink.

clue.text: Do they make ear-splitting noises ?

parts.note: ear-splitting means deafening, but threshing machines literally split ears of grain

explanation.walkthrough: Threshers separate grain from ears of corn, and also make a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Threshers are machines or workers that beat grain from the ears of cereal crops.

clue.text: Railway roundabout ?

parts.note: a roundabout is a road junction or fairground ride; on a railway it is the rotating platform that swings engines round

explanation.walkthrough: A locomotive drives onto the rotating platform and is spun to face the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: This railway device is a rotating deck used to swing locomotives round, much like a circular road junction.

clue.text: Might they be exchanged for red cents?

definitions.text: Might they be exchanged for red cents?

parts.words: Might they be exchanged for red cents?
parts.note: red cents means small coins, but red is Soviet, and the coins of Russia are swapped for kopecks

explanation.walkthrough: A 'red cent' is a trifling coin, but 'red' also means Soviet: a hundred Russian kopecks make one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency unit of Russia, divided into a hundred kopecks.

clue.text: This tile is useless for farmers we may conclude

indicators.note: the clue's 'This' stands for the answer, which with the word tile attached makes the farming word, so tile is the part taken away

parts.note: land useless for farmers is barren, infertile
taken as written

explanation.surface: A roofing tile is no good to people working the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' plus 'tile' make the word meaning barren; removing TILE from INFERTILE leaves the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce something is to reach it by reasoning, as when people conclude from evidence.

clue.text: Member of a white Masonic quartette

definitions.text: Member of a white Masonic quartette

parts.words: Member of a white Masonic quartette
parts.note: refers to the four white plumes in A.E.W. Mason's novel, a pun on Masonic as belonging to Mason

explanation.walkthrough: In A. E. W. Mason's novel The Four Feathers, a man is sent four white plumes as a charge of cowardice; 'Masonic' means Mason's.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the four white plumes in Mason's story is one of a quill-bearing bird's plumes.

clue.text: Firmly taken in hand by the Egg Marketing Board ?

definitions.text: Firmly taken in hand by the Egg Marketing Board ?

parts.words: Firmly taken in hand by the Egg Marketing Board ?
parts.note: gripped tightly, with a second sense from eggs: a batch laid together is a clutch, the board's business

explanation.walkthrough: A clutch is a set of eggs laid at one time; the Egg Marketing Board was a British body that sold eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasped tightly is what the word means, and eggs come in clutches.

clue.text: Is this charge for the tablecloth ?

definitions.text: Is this charge for the tablecloth ?

parts.words: Is this charge for the tablecloth ?
parts.note: restaurants levy a fixed fee per diner, and the word for it is also what a tablecloth does

explanation.walkthrough: A cover charge is a restaurant's flat fee per place setting; a tablecloth covers the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover is a place setting at a restaurant table, and the cover charge pays for it.

clue.text: A portion of lobster for the Buddhist novice

definitions.meaning: a pincer claw of a crustacean
a disciple or pupil of a guru

explanation.surface: Seafood is served to a young monk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crustacean's pincer and a pupil of a spiritual teacher, two separate words spelt alike.

clue.text: Perpetually heard in every direction

indicators.note: heard means the answer is pronounced like the phrase given

parts.note: in every direction is all ways

explanation.surface: Someone's voice can be heard from all sides without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL WAYS, said aloud, is the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at every time without end, constantly.

clue.text: Raise the back

definitions.meaning: to bring up or lift up, as a child or a head

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to bring up or lift, and the noun means the hind part.

clue.text: It's effected mechanically by 18

parts.note: the rotating railway platform at 18 turns an engine to face the other way, a complete about-turn done by machine

explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is the railway turntable, which spins an engine through 180 degrees: a literal about-face.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of direction or opinion, which a rotating platform performs on a locomotive.

clue.text: Strange chore for a painter

indicators.note: made strange, the letters of the next word are reordered

explanation.surface: A painter is given an odd task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges CHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used by artists in paint.

clue.text: French dramatist confounds Nostradamus for a start

indicators.note: to confound is to mix up, so the letters are jumbled
only the start of the prophet's name is used, its opening run, dropping the tail

explanation.surface: A French playwright is said to baffle the famous prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a start' keeps NOSTRAD, the first seven letters, and 'confounds' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Rostand was the French playwright who wrote Cyrano de Bergerac.

clue.text: Observations about foreign currency

parts.note: re means about or concerning
marks were the currency of Germany

explanation.surface: Comments are passed on money from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks are spoken comments or notes made on something.
